items.a: DeeWaanAI is a marketplace for AI pipelines — multi-step AI workflows you can create, buy, and sell. Every listing is certified through an automated security scan, AI triage, and blind human review before it can be purchased.

items.q: What is a certified AI pipeline?
items.a: A certified pipeline has passed three independent checks: a deterministic security scan of its prompts, an AI quality triage, and blind evaluation of its real outputs by multiple human reviewers who don't know who built it.
Paste the DeeWaanAI MCP server URL into any MCP-compatible client — Claude, ChatGPT, Kimi, Cursor, and others. You then create and use pipelines directly from your chat.

items.q: Do I need new API keys?
items.a: You bring your own LLM provider keys. Your pipeline runs go to your providers under your keys — DeeWaanAI orchestrates, it doesn't intercept.

items.q: Is my pipeline IP protected if I sell it?
items.a: Yes. Secret prompts are encrypted, never shown to human reviewers, never used for training, and the buyer receives usage rights, not your source prompts.

Nothing. During beta everything is free and marketplace listings are in free preview. At launch it is one flat $9.99 monthly subscription per account — no tiers, no seats, no per-run metering — and Pioneers keep the best terms we will ever offer.

Our first 100 beta members. Pioneers get a permanent badge, free access to the full product during beta, a lifetime discounted creator commission, and 3 invites each. Spots are limited by our human-review capacity — the scarcity is real, not marketing.

items.q: Can I share a pipeline with someone who uses a different AI app?
items.a: Yes. DeeWaanAI is an MCP server, so you each connect your own client — Kimi, Claude, Cursor, or any MCP-compatible app. You lend the pipeline to that one account: by default they can run it and keep the answer without ever reading your prompts, and their run uses their own API keys. Publishing stays with whoever created the work, whatever privilege the share carries.
Research Mode adds batch runs (up to 100 inputs in parallel) and pipeline chaining (feed one pipeline's output into another). It's available now behind a feature flag — request early access.

items.q: What can I do without paying?
items.a: Everything. Beta is the complete product at no cost: the custom pipeline designer with IF/WHILE loops and quality gates, Human-in-the-Loop approval gates, the AI Auto-Designer, up to 3 of your own LLM providers in one pipeline, and publishing to the marketplace. There is no trimmed tier to grow out of.

IF/WHILE loops let you build conditional and repeating workflow logic — included in the one subscription, not a paid extra. A quality gate can check an agent's output and automatically loop back until it passes — or route to a different step based on the result.

The AI Auto-Designer lets you describe your goal in plain language — for example, 'turn a product idea into a launch plan' — and the platform automatically generates the optimal pipeline with agents, prompts, quality gates, and approvals. It is included in the one subscription.

trust.metaDescription: Every DeeWaanAI marketplace listing passes a deterministic security scan, non-gating AI triage, and blind human review before it can be sold. Fail-closed by design.
trust.title: How DeeWaanAI certification works
trust.intro: Most AI marketplaces sell promises. DeeWaanAI sells proof. This page explains exactly what happens to a pipeline before it is allowed to be sold — and why.

paragraphs: Every AI marketplace has the same structural flaw: anyone can upload anything. A listing is a title, a description, and a promise. The buyer has no way to know whether the prompts are well-engineered, quietly broken, or actively malicious — until after they have paid.

Some platforms add AI judges. That helps, but an AI grading its peers is gameable: prompt-injection tricks and evaluator-pleasing fluff score well without being good. Others rely on creator self-reviews and star ratings, which measure popularity, not quality.
DeeWaanAI was designed around a different premise: trust must be earned by the pipeline, in three independent layers, before money can change hands.

The first gate is code, not AI. Every submitted pipeline passes through a deterministic scanner that inspects the actual prompt content for injection phrases, hidden Unicode tricks (zero-width characters, bidirectional overrides, homoglyphs), data-exfiltration patterns, embedded secrets, and PII leaks.

Because the scanner is deterministic, it cannot be charmed, confused, or prompt-injected. A listing that fails is rejected immediately, with the specific findings returned to the creator. No exceptions, no appeals to a language model's mood.

sections.h: Layer 2 — AI triage that advises, never decides
paragraphs: Next, the platform — not the creator, not the buyer — runs the pipeline against a suite of generated test inputs on a platform-controlled model. The triage scores quality across six dimensions and gives the creator fast, concrete feedback.

Crucially, the AI triage is non-gating by design. It can only stop a listing in one case: when quality is so low that sending it to human reviewers would waste their time. It can never approve a listing for sale. AI advises; it never decides. This removes the entire class of 'game the judge' attacks that plague AI-only review systems.

The final gate is the one that actually matters. Real outputs from the pipeline — not its prompts, not its marketing copy — are placed in a blind review pool. Independent reviewers score what they see without knowing whose pipeline produced it, what it's called, or how anyone else scored it.

Blindness is the mechanism that prevents collusion: reviewers cannot coordinate with creators they cannot identify, and self-review is impossible because the system, not the reviewer, assigns tasks. A listing becomes buyable only when multiple independent humans agree the outputs are genuinely good — measured as both an average score and a pass ratio, so one generous outlier cannot carry a weak pipeline.

Every layer errs in the same direction: if anything goes wrong — a scan error, a triage timeout, a missing review quorum — the listing simply stays unpublished. There is no failure mode in which a pipeline accidentally becomes sellable.
This is the opposite of how most platforms treat errors, and it is deliberate. Trust compounds slowly and collapses fast; the system is built to never spend trust it hasn't earned.

sections.h: What this means for creators' IP
paragraphs: Certification never exposes the creator's work. Secret prompts are encrypted at rest, are never shown to human reviewers (they see inputs and outputs only), and are never used to train models. What a buyer purchases is the right to run the pipeline — not the source prompts behind it.
The result is a marketplace where creators can sell their best work without giving it away, and buyers can purchase with something no other prompt marketplace offers: evidence.

privacy.metaDescription: What data DeeWaanAI collects, how it is used and stored, and the rights you have over it.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy

paragraphs: This Privacy Policy explains what information {{COMPANY_LEGAL_NAME}} ("we", "us") collects through the DeeWaanAI platform, website, and MCP server (the "Service"), how we use it, and the choices you have.

Account data: your email address, username, and authentication identifiers. Configuration data: pipelines, agents, and settings you create. Credentials: LLM provider API keys you choose to store, which are encrypted at rest and used only to call your providers on your behalf. Usage data: run logs, audit events, and technical telemetry needed to operate and secure the Service. Waitlist data: email address, selected role, and referral attribution when you join the Pioneer 100 waitlist.

We use collected data to operate the Service (including executing your pipelines with your providers), to certify marketplace listings, to secure the platform and prevent abuse, and to communicate with you about the Service. We do not sell your personal data, and we do not use your prompts or provider keys to train models.

Pipeline runs send the relevant prompts and inputs to the LLM providers you configured, under your own accounts and keys — this is the core function of the Service. We additionally rely on infrastructure processors (hosting, database, object storage, and payment processing when paid purchases begin) under appropriate data-processing terms.

We retain account and configuration data while your account is active. You may export your data at any time through the platform's data-portability tools, and you may request deletion of your account and associated personal data via {{FALLBACK_EMAIL}}. Backups rotate out on a fixed schedule after deletion.

Depending on your jurisdiction (including the UK and EEA), you may have rights of access, rectification, erasure, portability, restriction, and objection. Contact {{FALLBACK_EMAIL}} to exercise them. You may also lodge a complaint with your local data-protection authority.
We may update this policy from time to time and will post the revised version on this page with a new "last updated" date.
